enade-2021-cc-b-d05.notes: RESOLVED IN PHASE 1C (previously a confirmed structural failure in Phase 1B - see git history for the prior note). Root causes found and fixed (see docs/decisions.md, 'Phase 1C' ADR, and figures.py/assembler.py): (1) label absorption never excluded monospace lines, so the tree-diagram figure region grew ~110pt into the right-column code area, causing assembler.py's Y-range-only region-exclusion check to silently drop almost the entire heapify() function body; (2) that same exclusion check never verified horizontal (column) overlap at all, so even after fixing (1) it still swallowed right-column code sharing a Y-band with the left-column diagram; (3) MAX_LABEL_LINE_WIDTH (300pt, calibrated for single-column pages) never fires on this page's ~245pt-wide columns, so the statement's own opening paragraph (immediately following the question marker, directly above the diagram) was itself being absorbed as if it were a figure label. All three fixed via general, content-shape-based rules (exclude monospace from label candidates; require real X-overlap for region containment; protect genuine two-column body-text margins from absorption), not by hardcoding anything to D5's question id. Additionally, code reconstruction now preserves a real blank line (previously collapsed) between 'int e, d, max, aux;' and 'e = left(i);', detected from the run's own modal line pitch. Result, verified line-by-line against the rendered page: the opening paragraph, the array-table+tree-diagram figure (unchanged, already faithful), the second paragraph (heap-máximo definition + CORMEN citation + implementation intro), the COMPLETE code (left(), right(), the comment block, the complete heapify() body including the blank line and the nested if/aux-swap/recursive-call block, and the complete buildHeap()), and the final item a)/b) paragraph are all present, complete, and in the correct reading order (paragraph -> figure -> paragraph -> code -> paragraph). No truncated version is presented as complete. Per PROMPT section 22, D5 is promoted to verified: prose complete, code complete (not merely visual-primary), block order correct, figure preserved, asset legible, automatic_validation passes (Phase 1B's blanket code+multi-page distrust rule was removed - see validator.py - since the reconstruction it distrusted is now fixed and tested), visual_validation passes.

enade-2021-cc-b-q20.notes: RESOLVED IN PHASE 1C (previously two confirmed minor defects in Phase 1B - see git history for the prior note). Inspector: Claude (Sonnet 5), automated agent performing a documented visual comparison per PROMPT Phase 1C section 16, 2026-08-10. Page inspected: source PDF page 29 (data/raw/geacc-enade/2021/b1_prova.pdf), multiple crops at 8x-16x zoom. (1) GUTTER: root cause found - the printed line-number gutter ('1' through '26') is drawn as a narrow left column (x0~=29.7-31.9) distinctly separate from the code body (x0>=65.7); for 25 of 26 rows PyMuPDF already emits the gutter number as its own separate text line, correctly stripped by chrome.py's existing bare-1-3-digit rule; for exactly one row (11, 'int funcao2...') PyMuPDF instead fused the gutter number into the same physical line as the code ('\t11 \t int funcao2(...)'), which chrome.py's whole-line check cannot catch since the merged line is not purely numeric. Fixed generally (assembler.py's new `_strip_line_number_gutter`, tested in test_extraction_assembler.py): drops a purely-numeric gutter line, and for a merged line, strips a leading bare-integer-plus-whitespace prefix (a shape no real C statement has) and reconstructs the remainder's indentation from the run's own *other*, unaffected lines - never from the corrupted merged line's own x0. Verified: the rendered code now has zero gutter leakage anywhere (checked line-by-line) and 'int funcao2(...)' sits at the correct column-0 indent, matching its sibling function definition. (2) L/1 GLYPH: investigated with direct glyph-outline comparison, not just PyMuPDF's own decode - rendered 16x-zoom crops of every occurrence and of unambiguous reference characters in the same CourierNewPSMT 12pt font. Finding: the character in 'funcaol' (function definition, row 3) and in 'm+l' (row 18) both show a flat/horizontal top serif plus a horizontal base serif with NO diagonal flag - matching the unambiguous 'l' reference (the 'l' in '#include') and visibly different from the unambiguous '1' reference (a clear diagonal top-left flag, seen in 'TAM 10' and in BOTH other occurrences of 'funcao1' - the printf call on row 24 and the alternatives prose 'funcao1,' in item II). This is decisive typographic evidence, not an inherent ambiguity: 'funcaol' (with lowercase L) is genuinely how the function is spelled at its own definition, while it is called as 'funcao1' (digit 1) at both call sites - a real inconsistency in the source PDF's own typesetting/typography, not an extraction artifact. No second official source was needed (PROMPT section 8.3 only applies when internal evidence is insufficient - it was not here). The pipeline was already transcribing both characters correctly (as 'l') before this phase; the resolution is the disclosed forensic confirmation itself, not a text change. Per PROMPT section 23, Q20 is promoted to `verified` (not `verified_with_source_ambiguity`): the gutter was a pipeline defect, now fixed and tested; the l/1 question was resolved with typographic evidence, not left ambiguous.
